newsitem.title: CHINA: South China firms plan $1.4 bln IC chip plant.
newsitem.headline: South China firms plan $1.4 bln IC chip plant.

text.p: Two Chinese companies have agreed to form a consortium to build a $1.4 billion integrated circuit (IC) chip factory in Shenzhen city in southern China's Guangdong province, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Shenzhen-based telecommunications supplier Zhongxingxin Telecom Equipment Ltd and a local technology firm had signed an agreement to create the investment consortium for the project, which would require funding from nearby Hong Kong, it said.
The official agency gave no other details of the consortium or of how it would attract investment.
The planned plant would produce eight-inch chips of between 0.25 to 0.35 microns and would have a minimum monthly output capacity of 20,000 units, Xinhua said.

It gave no timescale for completion of the plant, which was expected to boost China's fledgling IC chip industry and raise the ratio of domestically-produced telephone switching systems and other electronics products.

Chip industry analysts say China is keen to promote the production of sub-micron IC chip plants but that development is hampered by import tariffs on vital foreign production equipment and U.S. high-technology export restrictions.
